stem: The principle of atomic bomb is based on –
expl: The principle of an atomic bomb is based on nuclear fission. Nuclear fission means the splitting of a heavy nucleus such as Uranium-235 and Plutonium-239 into two or more light-er nuclei. In this process, a very large amount of energy and additional neutrons are released.

stem: Nuclear fission occurs due to the collision of—

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Nuclear fission occurs due to the collision of neutrons. When neutrons are fired at atoms of a heavy element, the heavy element splits into lighter elements, as a result of which a very large amount of energy is released.

stem: Hydrogen bomb based on the principle of :

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / more than one of the above

expl: A hydrogen bomb is based on an uncontrolled nuclear fusion reaction, in which two or more small nuclei combine to form a larger nucleus, releasing a huge amount of energy.

expl: DO is made of two atoms of deuterium (D) and one atom 2 of oxygen (O). DO is known as heavy water. In nuclear reactors, heavy water (DO) is used as a moderator.

stem: Which of the following is not an electromagnetic wave?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: Electromagnetic waves include radio, microwave, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-rays, and gamma rays. Alpha rays are not included under electromagnetic waves. Alpha rays are a type of ionizing radiation.

stem: Which of the following is a positively charged particle emitted by a radioactive element?

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: An alpha particle is made up of two protons and two neutrons. High-energy electrons are known as beta particles. Clearly, an alpha particle is positively charged due to the presence of protons, whereas a beta particle is negatively charged due to the presence of electrons. Cathode rays are a stream of electrons emitted from the negative electrode (cathode) in a discharge tube containing gas at low pressure. A radioactive substance emits alpha, beta and gamma rays.

stem: The critical mass of a fissile material will be -

options.label: b
options.text: Minimum mass required for chain reaction

options.label: d
options.text: More than one of the above

expl: The critical mass of a fissile material is the minimum amount of fissile material that will support a self-sustaining chain reaction. At this mass, the neutrons released as products of one fission reaction can cause fission in neighboring atoms.
